title: Armenian Diaspora Repatriation Wave to Soviet Armenia
reason: The repatriation wave occurred 1946-1949, not 1950. Over 89,000 Armenians repatriated 1946-49 from Lebanon, Syria, France and other countries. The year 1950 is off by 1+ years from the core event.

title: Lake Sevan Water Level Reduction Begins Ecological Crisis
reason: The Sevan tunnel opened in 1949 and water level began dropping significantly from 1949 onward. By 1959 the level had dropped 13.7 m. The event year 1952 is plausible as a mid-crisis marker but the description says 'begins' — the reduction began 1949. Year is materially off.

title: Death of Stalin and Political Thaw in Soviet Armenia
reason: Stalin died March 5, 1953. De-Stalinization and political thaw in Soviet republics including Armenia is well-documented.

title: Matenadaran Institute of Ancient Manuscripts Opens
reason: The Matenadaran purpose-built building was completed in 1957 and the institute officially established in 1959. Year 1955 is off by 2-4 years.

title: Zvartnots International Airport Opens Near Yerevan
reason: Zvartnots Airport opened in 1961, not 1957. Year is off by 4 years.

title: Metsamor Nuclear Power Plant Site Selected
reason: Construction started in 1969 and Unit 1 went online in 1976. A 1960 site selection is plausible for Soviet planning timelines but no source confirms this specific year.

title: Byurakan CETI Conference Brings Carl Sagan to Armenia
reason: The Byurakan CETI conference was held September 6-11, 1971, not 1962. Year is off by 9 years. There was a 1964 Byurakan SETI conference but Carl Sagan attended the 1971 CETI event.

title: Mass Genocide Commemoration in Yerevan; First Public Protest
reason: April 24, 1965: approximately 100,000 protesters gathered at Yerevan Opera Theatre on the 50th anniversary of the Armenian Genocide. Well-documented as the first such mass demonstration in the USSR.

title: Tsitsernakaberd Armenian Genocide Memorial Inaugurated
reason: The solemn opening ceremony took place November 29, 1967, during the 47th anniversary of Soviet Armenia. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Metsamor Nuclear Power Plant Construction Begins
reason: Sources confirm Unit 1 came online December 22, 1976 and Unit 2 in January 1980. A 1969 construction start is plausible for Soviet nuclear timelines but no source directly confirms this year.

title: ASALA Armenian Secret Army Founded in Beirut
reason: ASALA was founded in 1975 in Beirut, not 1972. Year is off by 3 years. First acknowledged killing was October 1975.

title: Sergei Parajanov Arrested by Soviet Authorities
reason: Parajanov was arrested in December 1973 in Kyiv on charges of homosexuality and speculation. Well-documented.

title: Metsamor Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 Goes Online
reason: Unit 1 first generated electricity on December 22, 1976, not 1975. Year is off by 1 year.

title: Armenian Language Enshrined in New SSR Constitution
reason: Plausible — the 1978 Soviet republic constitutions are documented and Armenia did enshrine Armenian as state language — but no direct source confirms this specific provision's significance against Soviet pressure.

title: Karabakh Petitions Submitted to Moscow Amid Rising Tensions
reason: Petitions requesting transfer of Nagorno-Karabakh were submitted in the late 1970s. The specific year 1978 is plausible but not directly confirmed by found sources.

title: ASALA Paris Orly Airport Attack Kills Eight
reason: July 15, 1983 bombing at Orly Airport Turkish Airlines desk killed 8 people and wounded 55. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Gorbachev's Glasnost and Perestroika Reach Soviet Armenia
reason: Gorbachev came to power in March 1985 and introduced glasnost/perestroika policies which reached all Soviet republics including Armenia. Well-documented.

title: Chernobyl Disaster Intensifies Anti-Nuclear Movement in Armenia
reason: Chernobyl disaster was April 1986 and did intensify anti-nuclear sentiment in Armenia regarding Metsamor. Mass protests against Metsamor are documented.

title: Mass Karabakh Demonstrations; Over One Million in Yerevan
reason: Beginning February 1988, massive demonstrations in Yerevan over Nagorno-Karabakh unification. Wikipedia confirms over one million gathered at Opera Square.

title: Sumgait Pogroms Against Armenians in Azerbaijan
reason: Anti-Armenian pogroms in Sumgait, Azerbaijan, late February 1988, killing dozens and injuring hundreds. Well-documented.

title: Spitak Earthquake Kills Up to 50,000; Cities Destroyed
reason: December 7, 1988 magnitude 6.8 earthquake. Death toll 25,000-60,000 (upper bound is 50,000+ per many sources). Spitak and Leninakan/Gyumri severely damaged. Facts accurate.

title: Armenian SSR Declares Sovereignty over Soviet Law
reason: Armenian Supreme Soviet passed sovereignty declaration in 1989 asserting primacy of Armenian law. Confirmed.

title: Metsamor Nuclear Plant Shut Down After Earthquake Pressure
reason: Metsamor was shut down in early 1989 following the 1988 earthquake and public pressure. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Ethnic Cleansing; Armenians Expelled from Azerbaijan
reason: Mass expulsions of Armenians from Azerbaijan and reciprocal expulsions of Azerbaijanis from Armenia documented for 1988-1989 period.

title: Armenian National Movement Wins Soviet-Era Elections
reason: Armenian National Movement won May-June 1990 elections; Levon Ter-Petrosyan elected chairman of Supreme Soviet. Confirmed.

title: Armenia Declares Independence; 99% Vote Yes in Referendum
reason: Referendum September 21, 1991; 99.5% voted yes with 95% turnout. Ter-Petrosyan became first president. Confirmed.

title: Azerbaijan and Turkey Impose Energy Blockade on Armenia
reason: Azerbaijan and Turkey blockade of Armenia beginning 1992 is well-documented, cutting gas pipelines and rail.

title: OSCE Minsk Group Established for Nagorno-Karabakh Mediation
reason: OSCE Minsk Group created in 1992 by CSCE; co-chaired by Russia, France, and the United States from 1997. Confirmed.

title: Armenian Forces Capture Surrounding Azerbaijani Districts
reason: Armenian/Karabakh forces captured Kelbajar, Agdam and other surrounding districts in 1993, controlling ~20% of Azerbaijan's territory. Confirmed.

title: Armenian Dram Introduced as National Currency
reason: Armenian dram introduced November 22, 1993, replacing the Soviet/Russian ruble. Confirmed.

title: Bishkek Protocol Ceasefire Ends First Nagorno-Karabakh War
reason: Bishkek Protocol signed May 5, 1994; ceasefire effective May 12, 1994. Russian-brokered. Confirmed.

title: Armenia-Russia Treaty of Friendship and Military Basing
reason: Armenia-Russia Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation signed 1994, establishing Russian military base at Gyumri. Confirmed.

title: Armenian Constitution Adopted; Semi-Presidential Republic Established
reason: Constitutional referendum July 5, 1995; approved by 70.3% of voters; established semi-presidential republic. Confirmed.

title: Metsamor Nuclear Plant Controversially Restarted for Energy
reason: Unit 2 was restarted on November 5, 1995, not 1997. The event description says 'restarted in 1995 and by 1997 was providing ~40%' — the year label is 1997 but the restart year is 1995. The event year is off by 2 years for the restart itself.

title: Ter-Petrosyan Resigns; Kocharyan Assumes Presidency
reason: Ter-Petrosyan resigned February 3, 1998 under pressure over Karabakh peace compromise. Kocharyan elected president March 30, 1998. Confirmed.

title: France Officially Recognizes the Armenian Genocide
reason: The French National Assembly passed a bill May 29, 1998, but it became official law only on January 29, 2001 after Senate passage and presidential signature. The event is real but categorizing 1998 as 'officially recognizes' is misleading — official recognition came 2001.

title: Parliamentary Shooting; Prime Minister Sargsyan and Speaker Killed
reason: October 27, 1999 attack killed PM Vazgen Sargsyan, Speaker Karen Demirchyan, and 6 others. Confirmed.

title: Pope John Paul II Visits Armenia for 1700th Anniversary
reason: Pope visited Armenia September 25-27, 2001 for the 1700th anniversary of Armenian Christianity. Joint declaration with Catholicos Karekin II. Confirmed.

title: Kocharyan Re-elected in Disputed Vote; Protests Follow
reason: Kocharyan re-elected in February 2003 elections criticized by international observers; opposition protests followed. Confirmed.

title: Armenia Signs EU European Neighborhood Policy Action Plan
reason: The EU-Armenia ENP Action Plan was adopted November 14, 2006, not 2004. Year is off by 2 years.

title: Armenia-Turkey Football Diplomacy Opens Normalization Hope
reason: Football diplomacy began September 6, 2008, when Turkish President Gul attended the World Cup qualifying match in Yerevan — not 2007. The event year is off by 1 year.

title: Post-Election Violence Kills Ten in Yerevan; Crisis Year
reason: Presidential election February 19, 2008; March 1-2 crackdown killed 10 people (8 protesters, 2 police). Confirmed.

title: Global Financial Crisis Causes 14% GDP Contraction in 2009
reason: The financial crisis hit Armenia in 2008 with GDP contracting 14% in 2009. IMF data confirms ~14% contraction. Correct to attribute the cause to 2008 crisis.

title: Zurich Protocols with Turkey Signed but Not Ratified
reason: Zurich Protocols signed October 10, 2009. Faced strong Azerbaijani opposition and were ultimately not ratified. Confirmed.

title: Sargsyan Abandons EU Association Agreement for Eurasian Union
reason: September 3, 2013: Sargsyan announced Armenia would join the Eurasian Customs Union, abandoning the nearly-completed EU Association Agreement. Confirmed.

title: Electric Yerevan Protests Against Russian-Owned Utility
reason: The Electric Yerevan protests occurred in summer 2015, not 2014. Year is off by 1 year.

title: Armenian Genocide Centennial; World Leaders Gather in Yerevan
reason: April 24, 2015, centennial commemorations; Putin, Hollande and other world leaders attended at Tsitsernakaberd. Confirmed.

title: Constitutional Referendum Shifts Armenia to Parliamentary System
reason: December 6, 2015 referendum approved transition to parliamentary system with 63-66% support. Confirmed.

title: Four-Day War in Nagorno-Karabakh; Azerbaijan Advances
reason: April 1-5, 2016 clashes; ceasefire April 5. Azerbaijan gained ~8-20 km2. Over 100 soldiers killed on both sides (88 Armenian + 31-92 Azerbaijani). Confirmed.

title: Velvet Revolution Forces Sargsyan Resignation
reason: April 2018 protests led by Pashinyan; Sargsyan resigned April 23, 2018. Peaceful transition. Confirmed.

title: Pashinyan's Anti-Corruption Campaign Arrests Former Officials
reason: Kocharyan arrested July 27, 2018 on charges related to the 2008 post-election violence crackdown. Confirmed.

title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War; Armenia Suffers Catastrophic Defeat
reason: September 27 - November 10, 2020: 44-day war; Azerbaijan recaptured surrounding districts and significant Karabakh territory; ceasefire signed November 9-10. Confirmed.

title: November 2020 Ceasefire Cedes Karabakh Territory to Azerbaijan
reason: November 9-10, 2020 ceasefire required Armenia to cede all seven surrounding districts; Russian peacekeepers deployed. Confirmed.

title: Pashinyan Re-elected Despite War Defeat Demands for Resignation
reason: June 20, 2021 snap parliamentary election; Pashinyan's Civil Contract won 54% and 71 seats. Confirmed.

title: Azerbaijan Attacks Undisputed Armenian Territory; CSTO Fails to Respond
reason: September 12-14, 2022: Azerbaijan attacked Armenian sovereign territory; killed 207 Armenian soldiers; CSTO refused to provide military assistance, sending only a fact-finding mission. Confirmed.

title: EU Civilian Monitoring Mission Deployed to Armenian Borders
reason: EU Monitoring Capacity (EUMCAP) established October 17, 2022; became operational October 20, 2022. A permanent civilian mission (EUMA) was established January 2023. Confirmed.

title: Lachin Corridor Blockade Starves Karabakh Armenian Population
reason: Blockade began December 12, 2022; lasted through September 2023; caused acute shortages for ~120,000 ethnic Armenians. Confirmed.

title: Azerbaijani Offensive Ends Nagorno-Karabakh Republic
reason: September 19, 2023: 24-hour offensive; ceasefire accepted; republic dissolved January 1, 2024; over 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled. Confirmed.

title: Armenia Formally Suspends CSTO Participation
reason: Armenia froze CSTO participation on February 23, 2024, not 2023. In 2023 Armenia downgraded relations but the formal freeze/suspension announcement came in February 2024. Year is off by 1 year.

title: Armenia Ratifies Rome Statute; Direct Challenge to Putin
reason: Armenian parliament ratified the Rome Statute on October 3, 2023, not 2024. It entered into force February 1, 2024. The ratification event year is off by 1 year.

title: Armenian Parliament Votes to Pursue EU Membership Dialogue
reason: European Parliament passed resolution March 12, 2024 supporting Armenian EU candidacy; Armenian PM confirmed EU membership on political agenda September 2024; EU Integration Act passed March 2025. The 2024 framing is accurate.

title: Russia Withdraws Border Guards from Armenian Checkpoints
reason: Russia agreed in May 2024 to withdraw border guards; Zvartnots Airport departure July 2024; Armenia-Iran border checkpoint handed over December 30, 2024. Confirmed.
